maml:description.maml:para: Generates random passwords of a fixed length or of random lengths within a range.

The New-RandomPassword cmdlet generates random passwords and returns each one as a string. By default, it generates one password of 8 characters. Use -PasswordLength to set the length of every password and -Count to set how many passwords to generate, or use -MinimumLength and -MaximumLength instead of -PasswordLength to give each password a random length of its own.

Passwords are built from groups of characters. By default, the groups are the lowercase letters, the uppercase letters, the digits, and the symbols !@$#%&. Use -InputStrings to choose other groups of letters, digits, or symbols, such as groups that leave out characters that are easy to mistake for others, like l and 1, or O and 0. Use -ExtraCharacters to add groups of your own characters, and -OnlyUseExtraCharacters to build passwords from your own characters alone.

Every password holds a character from each group, and characters drawn from all the groups together fill the rest of it, where a character that two groups share is as likely as any other. A password with fewer characters than there are groups holds characters from a random choice of the groups instead. Last, the characters are shuffled, so the character from each group can be anywhere in the password.

Use -FirstCharacter to start every password with the same character. The character counts toward the length of each password, but it doesn't take the place of any group's character, and it always comes first.
Every random choice comes from the operating system's cryptographically secure random number generator.
Specifies the number of characters in each password, from 1 to 1,048,576. The length includes -FirstCharacter.
You can't use -PasswordLength with -MinimumLength and -MaximumLength.
Specifies the number of passwords to generate, 1 or more.

Specifies the least number of characters in each password, from 1 to 1,048,575. Each password gets a random length of its own, from -MinimumLength to -MaximumLength, both included. The length includes -FirstCharacter.
-MinimumLength and -MaximumLength are used together, and -MinimumLength can't be greater than -MaximumLength.
Specifies the greatest number of characters in each password, from 2 to 1,048,576. It can't be less than -MinimumLength.
Specifies the groups of characters that passwords are built from, in place of the default groups. Each value has to be one of these strings:
- abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz, the lowercase letters
- abcdefghijkmnpqrstuvwxyz, the lowercase letters except l and o
- ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ, the uppercase letters
- ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ, the uppercase letters except I and O
- 1234567890, the digits
- 234567890, the digits except 1
- 23456789, the digits except 0 and 1
- !@$#%&, six symbols
- !#%&, the same symbols except @ and $

Without -InputStrings, passwords are built from abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz, ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ, 1234567890, and !@$#%&, 68 characters in all. The parameter accepts each value regardless of case and uses it as you typed it. A group that's listed twice supplies two characters to every password that has room for them.
To leave out characters that are easy to mistake for others, such as l and 1, or O and 0, use the strings that leave them out, as in Example 5.
-OnlyUseExtraCharacters leaves out these groups.

Specifies more groups of characters to build passwords from, in addition to the default groups or the -InputStrings groups. Every password holds a character from each of these groups too, when it has room for one.

A string is one group, and so is a [char] or a [char[]]. Each element of a collection is a group of its own, so -ExtraCharacters 'abc', 'xyz' adds two groups, and -ExtraCharacters (Get-Content -Path .\groups.txt) adds a group for each line of the file. Any other value, such as a number, fails.

A group can't be empty, and it can't hold a control character, such as a tab, or a character that takes a surrogate pair, such as an emoji. A character that's listed twice in a group is as likely as the others.
Indicates that passwords are built from the -ExtraCharacters groups alone, without the default groups or the -InputStrings groups. The switch requires -ExtraCharacters.

Specifies the character that every password starts with. The character counts toward the length of each password, so -PasswordLength 1 gives the character alone, but it doesn't take the place of any group's character: the characters after it hold a character from each group, when they have room for one.

A number from 0 to 9, as in -FirstCharacter 5, is read as that digit, and other numbers fail. The character can't be a control character, such as a tab, or a character that takes a surrogate pair, such as an emoji.
You can't pipe objects to New-RandomPassword.
New-RandomPassword returns each password as a string.

maml:alert.maml:para: You can also run New-RandomPassword by its alias, rpas.

command:example.maml:title: ---------- Example 1: Generate a password of 12 characters ----------

dev:remarks.maml:para: The password holds a character from each default group: at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit, and one symbol.

command:example.maml:title: ---------- Example 2: Generate a password of a random length ----------

dev:remarks.maml:para: The password has from 6 to 67 characters. With -Count, each password gets a random length of its own.
The first positional argument is -PasswordLength, so each of the five passwords has 15 characters.

This command uses rpas, the alias of New-RandomPassword. The first positional argument is -PasswordLength and the second is -Count, so the command generates three passwords of 68 characters, and each one starts with %.

command:example.maml:title: ---------- Example 5: Leave out characters that look alike ----------

dev:remarks.maml:para: -InputStrings takes the place of the default groups. These groups leave out l and o, I and O, and 0 and 1, so no password holds them, and each password still holds a lowercase letter, an uppercase letter, a digit, and a symbol.

command:example.maml:title: ---------- Example 6: Add a group of your own characters ----------

dev:remarks.maml:para: -ExtraCharacters adds the symbols * + - = and ? as a fifth group, so the password holds at least one of them, besides a character from each default group.

command:example.maml:title: ---------- Example 7: Use only your own characters ----------

dev:remarks.maml:para: -OnlyUseExtraCharacters leaves out the default groups, so this command generates a PIN of six digits, all from the one group that -ExtraCharacters adds.
